title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation

content.problemStatement:
You're given a space-delimited sequence of tokens representing an
arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix notation). Each
token is either an integer or one of the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, and
in RPN an operator always applies to the two numbers immediately before
it.

**Evaluate the expression and return the result.**

Division between two integers truncates toward zero, not floor division.
constraints: each token is an integer in [-200, 200] or one of the operators +, -, *, /
the answer and all intermediate results fit in a 32-bit signed integer
division truncates toward zero, not floor division
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

hints: Can sorting the array simplify the problem, or does sorting take too long compared to a hash table lookup?
Consider two-pointer approaches if the array is sorted, or a sliding window if looking for contiguous subarrays.
Prefix sums or prefix XORs can answer range sum queries in O(1) time after O(N) preprocessing.
learningObjectives: Master core algorithmic concepts and pattern recognition for Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation.
Analyze time and space complexity trade-offs to meet optimal constraint benchmarks.
Formulate robust solutions addressing edge cases including boundary values and empty sets.
